ORAL ANSWERSTO QUESTIONS 
Rape of Swiss Diplomat 
*221. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether any breakthrough in the case of rape of a Swiss Diplomat having 
been abducted in her own car from the Siri Fort Auditorium parking on 14th 
October, 2003 has been achieved; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, what steps are being taken to nab the culprits; 
(d) what was the deployment of police personnel at the parking outside Siri 
Fort Auditorium on that day; and 
(e) if no policeman was posted there, the action taken against the 
concerned officers responsible for the lapse? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS-
(SHRI HARIN PATHAK): (a) to (e) A Stat ement is laid oji theTable of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) Delhi Police has. inter-alia, made the following efforts so far to nab 
the culprits: 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003J 
(i) Over 20 teams of seasoned and experienced investigators were 
deployed for the investigation and a massive manhunt was 
launched in which all the listed criminals with similar description and 
similar modus-operandi were interrogated and their movements 
verified. 
(ii)  Based on the descriptions given by the victim, computer portraits of 
the suspects were prepared and the same were given wide publicity 
through media/cable network for seeking information from public; 
(iii)  Chance finger prints developed from the vehicle were matched with 
available data bank of Delhi Police and sent to neighbouring States for 
comparison; 
(iv)  Photographs of 74 suspects were sent to the victim and she gave 
positive indication about some of  them who were examined/ 
interrogated at length; 
(v)  Blood samples of seven suspects identified by victim were sent for 
DNA test and matching at Centre for DNA Finger Printing and 
Development (CDPD), Hyderabad; 
(vi)  Combing operations around the place of occurrence, possible 
routes and points of escape were carried out in great detail; 
(viii)  Over 14,000 persons have so far been questioned which include 
2000 suspects who were interrogated at great length; 
(viii)  The investigation of the case has been transferred from the South 
District Police to a Special Investigation Team of the Crime Branch 
consisting of experienced and seasoned officers headed by an 
additional Commissioner of Police; and 
(ix)  A reward of Rs. 50,000/-, whic h was subsequently enhanced to Rs. 4 
lakh, has been announced for giving clue to apprehend the suspects. 
(d) and (e) Two Head Constables and two Constables under the 
supervision of one Inspector had been deployed for security of the parking lot 
where the incident occurred. All of them have been placed under suspension.

BPL families identified under SJGSY 
*223. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of BPL families identified under the Swamjayanti Gram 
SwarozgarYojana, State-wise; 
(b) the names of States which did not contribute their share of funds along 
with the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether there were large scale diversions and mis-utilization of the 
funds and if so, the number of complaints received in this regard, State-wise; 
and 
(d) the steps taken to check the deficiencies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL) (a) to (d) A Statement is 
laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) No specific survey has been conducted for identification of Below 
Poverty Line (BPL) families under the Swaranjayanti Gram Swarozgar 
Yojana (SGSY). However, during each Five Year Plan, the Ministry of Rural 
Development assists the State Government to conduct a BPL 
9 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003] 
Census with a view to identifying households living below the poverty line 
who could be assisted under various anti-poverty Programmes including 
SGSY implemented by the Ministry. Accordingly, the States/ UTs were 
advised to identify the BPL households for assistance during the Tenth Plan 
and to complete the BPL Census, 2002 by June 2003. However, due to the 
ruling of the Hob'ble Supreme Court on 5th May, 2003, in People's Union of 
Civil Liberties (PUCL) Writ Petition No. 196 of 2001, the State Governments 
have been advised not to finalise the BPL list until the next hearing of the case. 
The results of BPL Census (2002) are to be finalized after obtaining the 
directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard. The State-wise break up 
of BPL families as per 1997 Census is annexed. 
(b) The funds under the scheme are released to District Rural 
Development Agencies directly in two instalments. The first instalment is 
released without any formal request from DRDAs if the second instalment was 
released to them unconditionally in the previous year. The release of State share 
in the previous year is examined at the time of processing of proposals for 
release of second instalment. An amount equal to three times the shortfall in 
the release of State share in the previ ous year is deducted from the Central 
release of the second instalment in the current year. As per the reports of the 
State Governments available with the Ministry, the States of Andhra Pradesh, 
Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, 
Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal 
did not contribute their full matching State share cumulatively since inception to 
2002-2003 due to their difficult financial position. 
(c) No, Sir, no large scale diversion and misutilization have been 
reported. Neither complaints in this regard have been received by this 
Ministry from any State. However, as per Reports No. 3 of 2003 of 
Comptroller and Auditor General, some instances of diversion/ misutilisation 
of SGSY funds amounting to Rs. 58.39 crore in the States/ UTs of Andhra 
Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli, Daman and Diu, Goa, Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, 
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Mizoram, Orissa, Pondicherry, Tamil 
Nadu and West Bengal have been reported during the period of 1999-2002. 
10 

[17 December, 2003]       RAJYA   SABHA 
(d) State Governments and respect ive District Rural Development 
Agencies are regularly asked to utilize the funds as per the guidelines of the 
Scheme. Wherever cases of temporary diversion of funds come to light in the 
audit reports of the Chartered Accountants, the DRDAs are directed to recoup 
the funds.

Hydel Power Development Policy, 1998 
†*229. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN': 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had formulated the Hydel Power 
Development Policy in 1998; 
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that the construction of Small Hydel 
Projects were targeted to be boosted up under the policy; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether Government have made any assessment in respect of power 
generation capacity in the Small Hydro Power Sector; 
(e) if so, the quantum thereof; and 
(f) the number of projects that came in to existence since the formulation 
of the policy alongwith the existing power generation thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI ANANT GANGARAM GEETE): 
(a) to (f) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. With a view to  accelerating the pace of hydroelectric 
power development in the country, the Government formulated the Policy on 
Hydro Power Development in 1998.The aim of the Policy is to initiate measures 
to check the declining trend in the sh are of hydro in the overall energy 
generation in the country and to exploit the large hydroelectric potential 
available, especially in the North and North-Eastern region. The objectives of 
the Policy inter-alia include promotion of small and mini hydel projects. The 
small and mini hydel potential pan provide a solution for the energy problems in 
remote and hilly areas where extension of the grid system is comparatively 
uneconomical and also along the canal systems. Small hydro projects can be 
developed in a shorter time frame as well as with a lower capital investment. 
They also involve fewer

environment and rehabilitation and resettlement problems. Under this policy, 
all small hydel projects upto a capacity of 25 MW were transferred to the 
Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (MNES) to provide greater 
thrust for its development. 
(d) to (f) Hydro-electric Projects with  an installed capacity of less than 
25 MW come under the purview of the MNES. As per information provided 
by MNES, there is an estimated potential of about 15,000 MW in the country 
from Small Hydel Projects (SHP) upto 25 MW station capacity. So far, 4233 
small hydel potential sites aggregating about 10,324 MW capacity have been 
identified. 466 SHP projects (upto 25 MW) with aggregate capacity of about 
1530 MW have been set up which include 339 MW capacity commissioned 
after 1.4.1998. 196 projects aggregating to about 610 MW are presently under 
construction.

Amendments in Sections 406 and 498A of IPC 
*230. SHRl ABANI ROY: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that many families in India are suffering due to 
exaggerated allegations of harassment and dowry cases made by women against 
their husbands and other family me mbers involving them in criminal 
misappropriation and cruelty; 
(b) if so, the steps Government propose to take in this regard; 
(c) whether the Hon'ble High Court in a judgement on 19th May, 2003 has 
directed the Government to review and make suitable amendments in Sections 
406 and 498A of IPC; and 
(d) if so, the action Government have taken or propose to take on the 
judgement of the Court? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRl I.D. SWAMI): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
30 

[17 December, 2003]       RAJYA   SABHA 
(a) and (b) There is no information available with the Government to come 
to the conclusion that many families in India are suffering due to exaggerated 
allegations of harassment and dowry cases made by women against their 
husbands and other family members involving them in criminal 
misappropriation and cruelty. 
(c) and (d) The High Court of Delhi in its judgement dated 19th May, 2003 
in the case of Savitri Devi Vs. Ram Chandra and Others has recommended 
that marital offences under Section 498A/406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 be 
made bailable. If the parties decide to either settle their disputes amicably to 
salvage the marriage or decide to put an end to their marriage by mutual 
divorce, they should be allowed to compound the offences so that criminal 
proceedings do not chase them if they want to start their married life afresh or 
otherwise. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2003 introduced in Rajya 
Sabha on 22nd August, 2003 has inter alia a provision to make Secton 498A of 
the Indian Penal Code 1860 a compoundable one by inserting Section 498A in 
the table under sub-section(2) of Section 320 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1973 whereby it can be compounded with permission of the Court.

units 
 †  231.SHRI LAJPAT RAI †: 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN': 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted any committees at national level 
during the last three years for seeking suggestions for growth and expansion of 
units in various sectors of textile production in the country; 
(b) if so, the sector-wise (mill, powerloom and handloom) details of such 
committees and when each of the committees was constituted; and 
(c) the details of reports submitted by these committees? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SYED SHAHNAWAZ 
HUSSAIN): (a) to (c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The details of some of the important Committees constituted for all 
sectors of the textile industry are: 
(i) Steering Group on Investment an d Growth in Textile Industry under 
Chairmanship of Shri N.K. Singh was constituted on 9.11.2001. 
(ii) Expert Committee for Growth and Development of Technical 
Textiles—constituted on 4.7.2002. 
(c) The Steering Group on Investment and Growth in Textile Industry 
has submitted its Report to the Government. The important 
recommendations include: 
1. Extend the unbroken Central Value Added Tax (CENVAT) chain to the 
entire Textile sector and discontinue CENVAT credit on deemed basis. 
2. Apply 8% CENVAT for the entire Textile sector starting at the yarn stage 
for a period of 3 years of enabling modernization of the sector. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.

3. On synthetic filament yarns—Polyester Filament Yarn (PFY), Partially 
Oriented Yarn (POY) and PolyesterTexturisedYarn (PTY)— reduce excise 
rates from 32% to 24% in first year and 24% to 16% in second year. 
CENVAT on polyester—cotton and viscose— cotton blended yarn be 
brought at par. 
4. Continue the present excise exemptions to the genuinely 
disadvantaged sectors. Retain the Small Scale Industry (SSI) Excise 
Exemption/CENVAT exemption to the sectors like fabrics woven on 
handlooms, khadi, silk yarn, hand processing totally without the aid of 
power whose details are contained in the Report. 
5. Retain CENVAT at 16% on all man-made/synthetic fibres. 
6. Reduce customs duty from 25% to 5% on capital goods of man 
made/synthetic fibre/yarn industry and similarly on certain garment sector 
machinery. 
7. Domestic production of such machinery be exempted from CENVAT 
whose import is exempted from  Counter Vailing Duty (CVD). 
Weaving preparatory and critical garment machineries by exempted 
from CVD/CENVAT. 
8. Reduce customs duty on intermediates of synthetic fibres and yarns 
from 20% to 15%. 
9. Reduce customs duty on apparel grade wool and flax fibre from 15% 
to 5%. 
 
10. In view of our comfortable foreign exchange position, permit the 
Textile industry to  access External Commercial Borrowing for 
purchase of indigenous machinery by a suitable modification in the 
Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) for implementation of 
projects under the Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS). 
11. Announce the constitution of a Textile Industry Reconstruction Fund 
with a Corpus of Rs. 3000 crores for financial restructuring of the 
Textile industry. 
The Expert Committee for Growth and Development of Technical 
Textiles has in its Interim Report prepared an action plan for promotion

not specifically provide that presence of women police is necessary while 
arresting women during night hours by policemen. However, the Supreme 
Court in its judgment dated 15th October, 2003 in Criminal Application No.

State of Maharashtra Vs. Christian Community Welfare Council of India and 
others have issued directions to the arresting authority that while arresting a 
female person, all efforts should be made to keep a lady constable present but in 
circumstances where the arresting officers is reasonably satisfied that such 
presence of a lady constable is not available or possible and/or the delay in 
arresting caused by securing the presence of a lady constable would impede the 
course of investigation such arresting officer for reasons to be recorded either 
before the arrest

Rajya Sabha has inter alia, a proposal to add a new sub-section (4) to section 46 
Cr. P.C. to prohibit arrest of a women after sunset and before sunrise except in

Rise in juvenile crime and suicidal deaths in the country 
1595. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that juvenile crimes are on the rise; 

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether any guidelines have been issued by Government to handle juvenile 
crime cases; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by Government to check the rise in such crimes? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a) and (b) As per statistics compiled by National Crime 
Records Bueau (NCRB), a total of 8888,9267 and 16509 cases of juvenile 
crimes under Indian Penal Code were reported at all India level during 1999, 
2000 and 2001 respectively. For compiling statistics, the age criterion of 
juvenile was changed from 16 to 18 years in 2001, which led to high rise in 
number of crime in 2001. 
(c) to (e) The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 
which has replaced the earlie r Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 inter-alia deals with 
apprehension of juvenile in conflict with law; control of custodian over juvenile; 
bail of juvenile; information to parents, guardian or probation officer, inquiry by 
Juvenile Justice Board regarding juvenile; order that may be passed regarding 
juvenile; order that may not be passed against juvenile; proceeding under Chapter 
VIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure not competent against juvenile; no joint 
proceeding of juvenile and person not a juvenile; removal of disqualification 
attaching to conviction; special provision in respect of pending cases; probation 
of publication of name, etc. of juven ile involved in any proceeding under the 
Act; provision in respect of escaped juveniles; punishment for cruelty to 
juvenile or child; employment of juvenile or child for begging; penalty for giving 
intoxicating liquor or narcotic drug or psychotropic substance to juvenile or 
child; and exploitation of juvenile or child employee. In order to ensure speedy 
implementation of the new law on Juvenile Justice, the Central Government 
have framed Model Rules under the Act for the guidelines of State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations.

adopting new strategies to apprehend fugitives, extradition procedure, 
setting-up of fugitive investigation units and granting of legal status to Red 
Corner Notices etc. After deliberations the conference recommended that: 
(1) National points of contact for fugitive investigations be established With a 
view to providing mutual operational assistance in fugitive matters and 
exchange of reference information. 
(2) Member countries, which do not have dedicated fugitive units to co-
ordinate international and national searches, should consider 
establishing them. 
(3) Fugitive units engaged in international fugitive investigations 
should be in a position to communicate directly with each other to 
ensure especially the timely sharing of information. 
(4) To the extent permitted by national laws, the subjects of Interpol search 
requests (Notice and Diffusions) should be entered into national 
lookout systems. 
(5) Upon receipt of an Interpol search request, member countries should 
conduct checks in relevant databases and report any leads 
developed to the requesting country. 
(6) To the extent permitted by national laws, member countries should 
consider the Red Notice a valid request for provisional arrest. 
(7) Member countries should consider utilizing all legal options, 
including their immigration laws, to facilitate the surrender of 
wanted persons to other countries for prosecution or service of 
sentences. 
(8) Member countries support the idea of a Data Matching Project and 
should consider their participation in this project sponsored by 
Interpol Secretariat General/Fugitives Investigating Support Sub-
Directorate. 
(9) Member countries support the idea of an International Lookout 
System and recommend the initiation of a pilot project and working group 
to further develop the concept.

this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) and (b) National Thermal Power 
Corporation (NTPC) issued Request for Proposal (RFP) document to the 
qualified bidders for Kavas Gandhar Stations. This envisaged a pre-bid 
conference with the bidder, which was held on 15th and 16th May, 2003. Based 
on the interaction in the pre-bid conference RFP was reviewed and 
amendments to certain clauses/articles of RFP were issued to all the bidders. 
The details thereof and reasons therefor are given in the enclosed Statement. 
(c) No, Sir. 
(d) Do not arise in view of (c) above. 
Statement 
Amendments to certain clause/articles of RFP of NTPC 
I.Price Currency 
As per the RFP documents, the bidders for Services and Bidders for supply 
of Natural Gas are allowed to quote in INR only. 
As per the amendment, Bidders for supply of Natural Gas and Providing 
Services are allowed to quote in US $ of INR or combination of US $ and INR 
at their own choice. 
136 

[17 December, 2003]       RAJYA   SABHA 
2. Price Adjustment 
As per the RFP documents, the Prices are required to be quoted on FIRM 
price basis without any price adjustment. 
As per the amendment, a clause has been introduced allowing 15% of the 
contract price be subject to price ad justment to compensate Bidders for 
fluctuations in price of operating cost. 
3. Financial Evaluation 
As per the RFP documents the evaluation of the Financial proposal is to 
be carried out on NPV basis. 
As per the amendment the criteria for selection shall be the least 
delivered cost of Fuel Supply option from amongst RLNG and Natural Gas 
route as on the date of opening of Financial Proposal. 
4. Development Guarantee (DG) 
As per the RFP documents, the selected bidder is required to furnish a DG 
for a value of US$ 20 million and with validity up to commencement of the fuel 
supply. 
As per the amendment the DG value shall be of US $ 4 Million or INR 200 
Million for LNG/NG supply (US$ 1 Million or INR 50 Million for Providing 
Services) and the validity of DG shall be upto CP satisfaction date plus 30 
days. 
5. Conditions Precedent Provisions 
As the RFP Document encashment of DG was linked to Condition 
Precedent (CP) satisfaction. Bidders have perceived it as a Risk. 
The Provisions had been reviewed and amendments made on following 
principles: 
 The unilateral right to waive off its own CPs by NTPC has been deleted. 
 Right to encash Development Guarantee only in case CP is satisfied by 
NTPC. 
137 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003] 
6. Take or Pay in First Year 
In the RFP document, on Take or Pay (ToP) provision is envisaged in the First 
Year of supply {i.e. build up period). Many bidders have requested NTPC to 
provide ToP in the first year and acco rdingly the provisions of ToP is 
amended to include the same. 
7. Most Favoured Customer 
As per the RFP document, the Seller/Developer is required to offer the 
price and the corresponding terms, which were agreed with the other contracted 
customers if that contract price is lower than the price agreed with NTPC. 
The provision is amended to limit it to "the customers in India". 
8.The Interest Rate 
The interest rate for delayed payment in the existing bid documents have 
been specified as LIBOR. 
The interest rate for delayed payment has been amended as LIBOR +1% in 
case of Contract Price being in US$. 
9. Termination 
(i) As per the bid document, NTPC has the right to terminate the 
agreement if at any time during the operation of this Agreement, Buyer 
is not able to off-take LNG for a consecutive period of 3 Months, 
except where Buyer is not able to  off-take LNG on account of the 
occurrence of an event of Force Majeure. 
As per the amendment, this provision is deleted. However, to limit 
the ToP liability of NTPC in case of continuous non offtake of 
LNG the clause has been suitably amended. 
(ii) As per the existing bid document, in case of non-payment by 
NTPC, bidders have right to suspend the delivery, however no right 
has been provided for the bidder to terminate the agreement. 
The Article has been suitably amended allowing for Termination. 
138 

[17 December, 2003]       RAJYA   SABHA 
10. LNG Ships 
As per RFP document, ships for transporting LNG should be Indian Flag 
Ships. Bidders have expressed difficulty to the stipulation of the above 
provision. Based on clearance from Ministry of Shipping, the document has 
been amended stating that the LNG tankers, which are not Indian Flag 
Vessels, will be required to switch over to Indian Flag Vessles after the 
tonnage tax is introduced in India.

Accelerated Generation and Supply Programme (AG&SP) 
1657. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the Accelerated Generation and Supply Programme in the 
power sector initiated by the Centre; 
(b) the assistance extended to the State Governments under the scheme 
during the last 5 years amount, year and State-wise; 
(c) whether there is demand for implementing the programme during the 
Tenth Five Year Plan also; and 
(d) if so, the details and Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) The Accelerated Generation and 
Supply Programme (AG and SP) scheme was started by Government of India 
through Power Finance Corporation (PFC) in the 9th Plan. Under this scheme 
interest subsidy @4% was provided to St ate Electricity Boards (SEBs), State 
Generating Corporations (SGCs), State Power Departments (SPDs), State 
Utilities and Central Public Undertakings on disbursement made by Power 
Finance Corporation (PFC) for Renovation and Modernization (R and M), Life 
Extension, expeditious completion of generation projects, missing transmission 
links and System Improvements Schemes of State utilities which were 
languishing for wants of funds. A small sum of money was also provided as 
grant for studies to be carried out by State Electricity Boards. The aim of the 
scheme was to accelerate completion of ongoing projects and increase the supply 
from the existing facilities in the shortest possible time. 
(b) The State-wise disbursement made against the schemes identified under 
AG&SP Scheme during the last 5 years is given in the enclosed Statement 
(see below). 
(c) and (d) Based on the success of AG and SP during Ninth Plan period, 
Government has extended the scheme to Tenth Five Year Plan with the 
following modifications:- 
(i)  Interest subsidy has been reduced from 4% to 3%. 
150

milestones of reforms. 
(iii) The scope of assistance under AG and SP scheme has been restricted 
to State sector projects which increase generation of electricity.

Generation of Hydro-Electric Power 
1664. SHRI RUMANDLA RAAMACHANDRAYYA: Will the Minister 
of POWER be pleased to state: 
(A) whether hydro power is the cheaper and pollution free energy source; 
and 
(b) if so, the action proposed to produce more hydro generated power to light 
up every household at the earliest? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAY AWANTI MEHTA):(a) Yes Sir. Hydro power is a renewable, 
economic, non-polluting and environmentally benign squrce of energy. Hydro 
Power Stations have the inherent ability for instantaneous starting, stopping, load 
variations etc. and help in improving the reliability of the power system. 
(b) The benefits of hydro power as a clean, environment friendly and 
economically attractive source of energy have been sufficiently recognized. 
The need for is accelerated developmen t also comes from its capability of 
enhanced system reliability and economics of utilization of resources. 
The Government of India is accordin g a high priority to exploit the 
untapped hydro electric potential in the country to promote clean energy and 
correct the hydrothermal imbalance, and has initiated concrete measures to 
increase the hydro installed capacity in the country. A hydro policy was 
announced in August, 1998 for the development of hydro power 
incorporating several enabling steps and measures. The Hydro Policy among 
other things lays emphasis on basin wise development, evolving consensus on 
inter-State issues, mitigation of geological risks, simplified procedure for 
transfer of clearances, promoting joint venture arrangements etc. 
In order to accelerate the process of  survey and investigation of the new 
hydroelectric sites and to create a shelf of feasible projects which could be 
taken up for execution, the Central Electricity Authority has carried out a 
preliminary ranking study of the bala nce hydro sides to enable potential 
hydro developers to take up detailed survey and investigation, cost estimates 
and tentative tariff for the most attrac tive and viable schemes in each basin in 
a phased manner. ' 
165 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003] 
Through a process of countrywide consultation, 162 hydro-electric schemes, 
with an estimated capacity of 50,560 MW, have been indentified for preparation 
of feasibility studies. This initiative for tapping 50,000 "* MW of hydro 
power was launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on May 24,2003 and will 
pave the way for the creation of a shelf of project which will be implemented 
in the next two Five Year Plans. This exercise is being undertaken by various 
organizations under the overall coordination of CEA. 
The Pre-Feasibility Report (PFRs) w ill provide useful information to 
prospective developers for taking up detailed Survey and Investigation and 
DPR formulation and facilitate the accelerated development of balance Hydro 
Electric Potential in the country. This is considered essential to generate a 
shelf of project which could be taken up for execution during Eleventh and 
Twelfth Plan and beyond. 
The Govt, has also approved a three stage clearance procedure for al hydel 
projects to be executed by the Central Public Sector Undertakings in consultation 
with the Ministries of Finance and Environment and Forests. This procedure 
will help in avoiding time and cost over-run of projects. 
Exemption to Mega Power Projects 
1665. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of 
POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that in 1999, Government had announced Mega 
Power Project Policy according to which the Thermal Power projects having a 
capacity of 1000 MW or more and selli ng power to more than one State are 
exempted from all customs and other duties levied by Government: 
(b) if so, the details of unis which have come up under this policy and the 
exemption that the Government has given to such units since 1999, year-wise 
and unit-wise; and 
(c) the details of projects notified by Government under "Mega Power 
Project Policy"? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATIJAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) The revised Mega Power Policy of 
166 

[17 December, 2003]       RAJYA   SABHA 
the Government of India was announced in November , 1998 which provides 
for zero customs duty for import of capital equipment for 19 identified inter-
State mega power projects. In additi on, the income-tax holiday has been 
continued with the provison that the tax holiday period of 10 years can be 
claimed by a promoter in any block of 10 years within the first 15 years. The 
enabling notifications under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962 
(52 of 1962) were issued during 1999 and 18 identified projects which had a 
capacity each of 1000 MW or more in the case of thermal projects and 500 
MW or more in the case of hydroelectric projects, have been notified for 
waiver of cutoms duty on import of capital goods. One of the identified 
projects viz., the Chamera-ll Hydroelectric Pr oject was not notified for the 
customs waiver benefits since its capacity was less than 500 MW. 
In addition to the above, the Si pat Super Thermal Power Project 
(4x660MW) being implemented by the National Thermal Power Corporation 
(NTPC) in Chhattisgarh has been accord ed mega power project status by the 
Government of India in December, 2001. The enabling customs notification 
for the Sipat project has been issued in 2002. 
(b) No mega power project has been commissioned so far. 
(c) Details of the above mentioned mega power projects notified for the 
customs duty exemption are given in the Statement (See below). As per the 
latest amendment to the Customs Notification issued in March, 2003, the 
customs duty waiver has since been extend ed to all inter-State projects which 
fulfill the basic criteria of minimum capacity of 1000 MW for thermal and 500 
MW for hydel projects subject to certification by the Ministry of Power.

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL) (a) to (e) Land and its management falls under 
the exclusive administrative and le gislative jurisdiction of the State 
Governments under Entry No. 18, List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule of

Mission 
1685. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Eighth Plan outlined an enhanced role for local bodies in the 
Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission (RGNDWM); 
(b) if so, details of RGNDWM missioned through local bodies for last three 
years, year-wise, state-wise and category-wise; and 
(c) the details of grant received and u tilized along with task under taken 
by RGNDWM on data collection and assessment of water availability, estimation 
of recharging potential for ground water regimes, desjgning rain water 
harvesting structures and enlisting community participation for decentralized 
water management, for last three years,  state-wise, category-wise and year-

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNA SAHEB M.K. PATIL): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) Water is a State subject. Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the states by rendering financial assistance under a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme namely Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programe (ARWSP). The 
programme has been revamped to institutionalise commuity based, demand 
driven Rural Water Supply programme. 20% of the outlay under ARWSP is 
earmarked for implementing projects based on the following three basic reform 
principles: 
* adoption of a demand-responsive a nd adaptable approach based on 
empowerment of villagers to ensure their full participation in the 
project through a decision making role in the choice of scheme design, 
control of finances and management arrangements. 
* Shifting of role of Government from direct service delivery to that of 
planning, policy formulation, monitoring and evaluation and partial 
financial support. 
* Partial capital cost sharing, either in cash or kind or both, and 100% 
responsibility of O and M by users. 
The powers to plan, sanction, implement and execute rural water supply 
schemes vest with State Governments. States can utilize ARWSP funds, inter-
alia, on assessment of water availability, estimation of recharging potential for 
ground water regimes, designing rainwater-harvesting structures etc. The 
details of the amount utilised separately for these aspects by States are not 
maintained at the Central level. The State-wise details of the amount released 
during the last three years are given in the statement.

Debt Restructuring Package for Textile Mills 
1687. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
SMT. AMBIKA SONI: 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have approved a debt restructuring package for 
integrated textile mills and a modernization scheme for the power loom 
sector; 
(b) if so, to what extent this new revival scheme for textile units has 
benefited the sick textile mills; 
(c) whether Centre has also decided to take steps to make the Indian textile 
and apparel sector competitive and felt the need to develop and popularize 
strong Indian brands, especially in readymade garments; and 
(d) if so, what are the main proposals that are being considered in this 
regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES 
(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) This package does not apply to sick units but to potentially viable 
textile units/mills having a minimum debt exposure of Rs. 2 crore. 
(c) and (d) The Government has taken various steps to make the Indian 
textile and apparel sector competitive which include: 
(i) Completion of CENVAT chain in entire Textile Value Chain with 
simultaneous rationalization excise duty on fibres, yarn, fabric/ made-
ups and readymade garments (RMG) in Union Budget 2003-2004. 
205 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December l2003] 
(ii) Launch of Cotton Technology Mission for boosting production and 
quality of cotton. 
(iii) A programme has also been launched to induct 50,000 shuttleless looms 
and to modernize 2.5 lakh powerlooms in the decentralised sector by 
2004. 
(iv) Announcement of a package for restructuring of debt portfolios of 
potentially viable textile units having debts exposure of Rs. 2.00 crores 
and above. 
(v) The Government had de-reserved the woven segment of readymade garment 
from the (Small Scale Industry) SSI sector. It has also raised the SSI 
investment limit for knitted segment to Rs. 5 crores. 
(vi) The Technology Upgradation fund Scheme (TUFS) has been made 
operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and 
upgradation of the sector. 
(vii) Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered under 
TUFS, have been extended the fac ility of accelerated depreciation at 
the rate of 50%. Cost of machinery has also been reduced through Fiscal 
Policy measures.This further encourages modernisation. 
(viii) With a view to making fabric production competitive, the custom duty 
on shuttleless looms has been reduced to 5%. 
(ix) National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its six branches and 
Apparel Training and Design Centres (ATQCs) are running various 
courses/programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements of textile 
industry especially apparel in the field of design, merchandising and 
marketing. 
(x) Facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories have been created to enable 
exporters to get the garments/textiles pre-tested for conforming to the 
requirements of importing countries. 
(xi) The Government has launched a centrally sponsored scheme titled 
"Apparel Park for Export Scheme" for imparting focused thrust for 
setting up of apparel manufacturing units of international standards at 
potential growth centres and to give fillip to exports.

scheme Textile Centre Infrastructure Development Scheme" (TCIDS) 
has been launched.

financial assistance to Textile Export Promotion Councils under 
marketing Development Assistance (MDA) Scheme.

international price and price expecta tions pertaining to cotton etc. The 
quantity of cotton, which has been exported from India is insignificant 
compared to the estimated total production of cotton in the country.

restrictions and cotton prices are guided by market forces.

Support package for jute industry 
1689. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have announced a support 
package for the jute industry with higher subsidy on capital investment of 20 
per cent; 
(b) if so, the details of the proposal announced by the Government; 
(c) whether Government are encouraging the production of Geo Textile with 
wider marketing network in India and overseas market; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES 
(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Jute Manufactures Development Council (JMDC), a statutory body 
under the aegis of Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, created through an 
enactment of the Parliament has launched the "JMDC Incentive Scheme for 
Modernization of Jute Industry" w.e.f. July 2002. The subsidy under the scheme 
was universally restricted to 15% of  the cost of machinery/equipment 
procured by the jute mills till September 2003. However, subsidy has been 
enhanced to 20% w.e.f. 19th September 2003 for establishment of new modern 
jute mills in new locations pertaining to jute growing areas having inadequate 
jute processing facilities after payment of cess for at least 3 months. 
However, the capital subsidy @15% of the cost of machinery and equipment 
is till admissible to modernization of existing units in areas having jute 
processing facilities. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) Government is encouraging the production of Geo Textiles in the 
domestic as well as international markets through: 
(i) Organising events such as the International Jute Symposium 
(February, 2003 at Kolkata), the National Seminar on Geo-textiles and 
Innovative Jute Products (August, 2003, at New Delhi); 
(ii) Sponsoring research activities for development of geo-textiles in 
research Institutes like Indian Jute Industries Research Association, 
208 

[17 December, 2003]        RAJYA   SABHA 
(IJIRA) Kolkata and Institute of Jute Technology (IJT) Kolkata. 
(iii) Encouraging and subsidising pa rticipation of manufactures of geo-
textiles in national and international fairs. 
(iv) Sponsoring Pilot Rural Roads Project for standardising the 
specifications for the use of jute geo-textiles in construction of rural roads under 
the Prime Minister's Gramin Sadak Yojana jointly with the National Rural 
Roads Development Agency, Ministry of Rural Development and the Central 
Road Research Institute, New Delhi. 
(v) Making technical presentations on Jute Geo Textiles to the concerned

(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) The Technology 
Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) is a dynamic Scheme in which 
amendments are made on a continuous basis in order to making it industry friendly.

which significant ones are given in statement (See below).

Statement 
Significant amendments made under TUFS since inception of the scheme. 
* Loans, which have been sanctioned prior to 1.4.99 but not disbursed, 
are considered under TUFS, if otherwise project meet the parameters of 
TUFS.

1.4.99 are considered under TUFS.

of downstream value addition capacity.

subject to a maximum expired life (vintage) of 10 years. 
* Air Jet, Water Jet, Projectile and Rapier looms with 10 years 
vintage and with a residual life of minimum 10 years. 
* Worsted sector machinery with 10 years' vintage and with a 
residual life of minimum 10 years. 
* Computerised flat bed knitting machine with 5 years vintage and 
with a residual life of minimum 10 years.

decentralised powerlooms sector.

addition activity for spinning capacity creation.

by other sources (other than bank loan) covered under TUFS subject 
to certain conditions. 
* An option of 12% Credit Linked Capital Subsidy provided to SSI 
textile units. 
* New units set up for manufacturer of compact yarn have been exempt 
from the stipulations of MES and downstrem value addition norms. 
* Relaxation in norms for cash profit, promoter's margin, debt equity ratio 
and revaluation of assets in respect of weak but potentially viable sick 
mills. 
* Waiver of minimum stipulated width of 165 cms in respect of semi-
automatic/automatic looms for decentralized powerloom sector. 
* Fibre dyed yarn as an eligible downstream value addition process for 
expansion of spinning capacity.

improving the qualitative and quantitati ve cocoon/raw silk production by

linguistic problems which will definitely pose a serious threat to the unity and 
integrity of the country.

Home Minister, Shri V.C. Shukla, assu red the House that in addition to 
English, all national languages listed in the Eighth Schedule would be 
introduced simultaneously as medium for -UPSC and other examination. Now 
that assurance has been violated. Again, the Government is trying to impose 
Hindi for conducting the Defence Services examinations.

tension, which is avoidable. The peop le of Tamil Nadu, cutting across party 
lines, will resist any move to impose Hindi like this. On behalf of the 40 crore 
non-Hindi speaking Indians, I demand th at the Defence Minister should roll 
back the proposal of conducting the examination only in Hindi and introduce all 
the Indian languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution to be the 
medium for conducting the examination. Thank you.

Need to provide drinking water and other facilities in primary schools of 
the country 
SHRI R.S. GAVAI (Maharashtra): Re spected, Madam, according to the 
Sixth All India Educational Survey Report, there are about 3,51,389 rural 
primary and upper primary schools in the country, which do not have drinking 
water facility for the students. Out of these 23,723 such schools are located in 
my home State Maharashtra alone. In these sc hools, children of very tender 
age, generally below ten years, belonging to the poor families mostly of farmers 
and farm labourers living in the villages go for schooling. We can only imagine 
the agony of these children who do not get drinking water even during the 
scorching summer under heat wave conditions in most parts of the country. It 
is a pity that we have failed in providing this basic necessity of life to these 
toddlers who have to remain thirsty while in school. No doubt, Governments 
have done their best to spread literacy in the country including the rural parts of 
the country, but priority has to be given to the basic infrastructure like pucca 
building, drinking water, toilets, boundary wall, playground, etc. Out of these, 
drinking water has to be given the uppermost priority. 
I, therefore, urge upon the Government to  accord the top most prioty to 
provide the facility of drinking water to the children of primary and upper 
primary schools of the country; and for this  purpose special Central Grants be 
given to the States so that this basic facility is made available to the poor 
students. I hope, the Central Government will start this right from the current 
finacial year and the coming Budget will certainly focus on this issue. Thank 
you.

Request for continuance of the centre of the central institute of fisheries 
education at Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh 
SHRIMAT IVANGA GEETHA (Andhra Pradesh): Madam, the Kakinada center 
of Central Institute of Fisheries Education, Mumbai was established in 1968. The 
Centre is supported with two fish farms, i.e. Brakishwater Fish Farm at 
Kakinada, and, Freshwater Fish Farm at Balabhadrapuram in East Godavari 
District. It is one of the nodal centres imparting short- 
260 

[17December,2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
term training extending technical guidance, developing research activities 
and transferring technologies to various aqua farmers. , 
Madam, nearly 3000 participants were imparted training through this centre. 
It has given rebirth to aqua farmers in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh by 
developing the eco-fridnely good menge pr actice by avoiding antibiotics and 
using probiotics rationally in shrimp culture prawns to avoid the refusal of 
shrimp exports to the European market with a reason of antibiotic residues. 
To meet the demand for air breathing fish seed, the centre has developed 
a new model hatchery technology and supplied the air breathing fish seed to the 
farmers, which has led to a boom in fresh water fish farm sector. Andhra Pradesh 
is having 976 km coastal line having vast potentiality of fish production. Fish is 
being exported to different States in the country like West Bengal, Assam, etc. 
Andhra Pradesh coastline is also famous for crab centre, which is a rare 
function of fisheries production. In addition to fish and prawn culuture, prawn 
production both off and on shore is being taken up on a large scale, which is 
having complementary research facility. In view of the long-standing research 
function, the Central Instit ute of Fisheries Education is highly required, and, 
also the importance of the fish produc tion in the coastal areas of Andhra 
Pradesh. 
The decision to close down the research centre will be detrimental to the 
fishermen's economy of the coastal An dhra Pradesh . Hence, I request the 
Union Minister of Agriculture to take an early action for the continuance of 
CIFE at Kakinada itself.

Need to check increase of HIV/AIDS patients in India 
DR. NARAYAN SINGH MANAKLAO (Nominated): Respected, Madam Deputy 
Chairperson, my Special Mention is r egarding HIV/AIDS patie nts. It is an 
undeniable fact that there are a large number of HIV/AI DS infected patients in 
India. According to some surveys, we are one of the high incidence category 
countries in the world. Prevention appears to be the only realistic option 
available now. But, for the purpose of prevention, awareness about AIDS is 
the key. Voluntary disclosure of HIV po sitive status from the patients and 
sufficient community support towards their treatment and rehabilitation are 
called for. For planning future action, we need to measure the magnitude of the 
problem. But, severe social stigma attached with AIDS patients is discouraging 
even educated patients from disclosing their HIV status. Even for the Church, 
one of the most progressive social inst itutions, the situation is no better. The 
national press has reported that on December 1 .which was also World AIDS Day, 
in Kerala, a 38 year old AIDS victim's dead body was not allowed to be buried in 
local cemetery by authorities.This is not an isolated incident. A fear psychosis is 
pervasive today among HIV positive community. If not immediately and 
effectively checked, this will adversely impinge on our developmental efforts. 
Therefore, I urge upon the Government to take sufficient steps to remove 
prejudices and misconceptions among the population at large regarding AIDS 
patients and to make sure that no patie nt is victimised, discriminated on 
segregated because of AIDS in this country.

SHRI T.S. BAJWA (Jammu and Kashmir): Madam, the condition of people 
living in the border areas all along the LOC/LAC in Jammu and Kashmir is

they be compensated by offer of a Government job to a member or nearest kin of 
the victim's family so that they have a permanent source of income and can lead 
a decent life. I urge upon the Government of India to give a serious thought to 
my proposal.

Plight of Tea Plantation Workers 
SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA (West Bengal): Madam, I am trying to raise 
a Special Mention which concerns millions of plantation workers throughout the 
country. I will be confining myself to West Bengal only. Its caption is "Tea 
Plantation Workers in Peril". 
Madam, the tea industry of West Ben gal is the second largest in the 
country. There are around 343 gardens sp read across the Dooars, Terai and 
Darjeeling hills. A majority of the tea plantations in the region are large 
production units of more than 400 hectares, covering an average area of 61.6 
per cent and manged and owned by big tea corporates. 
The plantations are not just economic units, but, to a large extent, control 
and regulate lives of a workforce of almost 3 lakhs, most of whom are from tribal 
regions of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Orissa and Madhya Pradesh. 
These workers live and work exclusively for their respective plantations, 
without any freedom of choice in terms of work and place of living.They are 
completely dependent on plantation management for food, water, shelter, 
education, health and sanitation. 
The tea industry is in an unprecedented crisis for years. At present, in West 
Bengal along nearly 23 gardens have been closed or abandoned rendering nearly 
25,000 workers jobless and exposing them to severe misery and completely 
collapsing their basic amenities for living. 
Even the chidren of these workers are forced out of schools and being 
engaged as child labours in available hazardous jobs without any choice. 
Malnutrition deaths have been rampant. A spectre of uncertainty is looming 
large. The social fabric is in peril in that particular zone. 
The State Government alone cannot manage such gruesome situation. 
Hence, I urge upon, through you, Madam, the Government of India to 
immediately resort to well-meaning measures to save the lives of nearly a lakh 
of poor people, most of them belong to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled 
Tribes. Such action should be undertaken on war footing. 
Madam, once again, with your permission, let me make an appeal to you. 
There are 30 Special Mentions which have been made today. But,

SHRI DRUPAD BARGOHAIN (Assam) Mr. Vice-Chair man, Sir, it is very 
pathetic that some innocent people from Bihar, Assam and other North 
Eastern States have suffered from rioting ar ising out of the recruitment policy of 
the North Frontier Railways by the Railway authorities, including the hon. Railway 
Minister. All of us condemn such rioting and sympathise with those families 
which have suffered and demanded from the Government to give suitable 
compensation to such families. Why have such incidents occurred in Bihar and 
Assam in particular? What are 
307 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003] 
the reasons? The most important reason is, the severest unemployment problem 
that is looming large in all the States of the country. The vision of our respected 
Prime Minister to create one crore- employment opportunities annually has also 
not worked. The State Governments are also callous in this regard. 
There were some vacancies in the Railways. Some aspirants for those 
posts had pitted themselves against each other. In one examination centre spot at 
Guwahati, some candidates of Assam had wrongly assaulted a few 
candidates who came from Bihar. As the Press report says, the Railway 
Minister reacted sharply by saying that those who were assaulted would be 
allowed to sit in the examination in Bihar, which led to indignaion in Bihar and that 
further led to' attacks on the innocent  people of the State of Assam and other 
North Eastern States, at Katihar, Barsoi and Jamalpur Railway stations, by some 
mobs, while they were travelling in trains. 
These events created further indignat ion and anger which led to attacks 
on innocent Bihari people in Assam.There was great friendship between the 
Assamese and Bihari people in Assam. But the mishandling of the railway 
recruitment policy by the Railway authorities led to such a misunderstanding 
among these people which is very very unfortunate. 
Secondly, the Railway Minister and other responsible Railway authorities 
repeatedly stated that because of the Supreme Court's verdict no reservation 
could be brought in the Railway recruitment system. On the other hand, the 
people of different States want reservation in certain categories of Railway 
Services. For example, in C & D categories of Railway Services, reservations 
are made for local people up to hundred per cent. When such sentiment were 
there, the Railway Authority went against this reservation, on the basis of the 
Supreme Court verdict, instead of being sober in delaing with the situation. This 
added fuel to the fire. Here lies the mishandling of the recruitment policy by the 
Railway Authority, So, the Railway Authority, particularly, the Railway Minister 
must take responsibility for this. 
Moreover, in Assam, another sentim ent arose when the people of Assam 
saw earlier that most of the appointme nts in the North-Frontier Railway had 
been done from Bihar—this has already been stated by Shri Dipankar 
Mukherjee—and these  appointees took their chairs in

different railway stations; according to some estimate, there was about 90 per 
cent of such appointees from Bihar. 
Sir, further, special recruitments in certain cases are there for the North-
Eastern States, particularly, in the Defence Forces. The previous United Front 
Government as well as the present NDA Government had also recognised the 
special situation which prevailed in this  region. Under such a situation, the 
Railway Authority should not overemphasise the Supreme Court verdict on 
recruitment for Central institutions. 
Sir, I urge upon the Prime Minister to look into all these matters seriously 
so that communal rioting does not take  place and national integration is not 
hampered with. 
Moreover, while the vacancies of C and D categories of the Railway Service 
should be reserved hundred per cent for t he people of the States where these 
vacancies occur, some reservations for the A & B categories also should be 
made. 
Sir, the paramilitary forces are necessary to control rioting. But that is not 
the only point. Unless you find out the real cause of rioting, unless you eradicate 
the root-cause, as I expressed during my speech, you cannot expect a 
solution. A solution can be found only when everybody underst ands what is in 
the mind of the people and what is the reality and objectivity of the situation in 
any State. Our Central leaders should understand these things very clearly. 
Otherwise, no solution can be there. Thank you, Sir. 
SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH SHARMAH (Assam): Sir, first of all, I want to 
condemn what happened last month in Assam and Bihar. The episode was, 
particularly, unfortunate, in Assam, t he State that has been suffering from 
chronic insurgency for the last two decades. During the last two-and-a-half 
years, under the present GovernmeriFof Assam, under the leadership of our Chief 
Minister, Shri Tarun Gogoi, there has been a perceptible improvement in the law 
and order situation. The militant outfits have been virtually marginalized as they 
have lost support of the masses, who want peace and tranquility in this State. 
The State was on its way towards reconstruction and development of the 
economy putting behind terror and turbulence of the past. This optimistic 
scenario has been repeatedly shaken and disturbed by the recent 
incidents.The insurgent 
309 

RAJYA SABHA [17 December, 2003] 
groups like the ULFA found a much-sought-after excuse to raise their heads 
and they indulged in killing, arson, etc. in the State.  This may have the effect 
of putting the clock back on the development efforts being undertaken by the 
State Government. Sir, it is, in this context, I feel strongly that without beating 
about the bush, and indulging in blame game, the core issue, the root-cause of 
incidents of violence has to be addressed, and I strongly feel that unemployment 
in the region, particularly in the State of Assam, where more than 16 lakhs of 
educated youth are seeking jobs, is t he root-cause of these incidents. And the 
wrong Railway recruitment policy is another cause for these incidents in Bihar and 
Assam. 
Sir, in this connection, I would like to give some figures which will expose 
the blatant injustice and discrimination against Assam in Railway recruitment. In 
the North- Eastern Frontier Railway, the length of railway line is 3,397 kms., out 
of which 2,529 kms., that is, 64.33 per ce nt, fall in Assam. As against this, out 
of a total staff strength of 71,052 in  the NF Railway, only 12,053 employees, 
that is, 16.97 per cent, are from Assam. This includes all bona fide residents 
of Assam, including the Assamese, Biharis, Bengalis, etc.The NF Railway has 
about 700 officers, out of which only 45, that is, 6.42 per cent, are from Assam. 
I would now give you figures relating to Bihar's share. Now, 363 kms. of NF 
Railway line falls in Bihar, which is, 9.28 per cent, and against this, 17, 776 
employees, that is, 25.2 per cent, are from Bihar. These figures reveal a clear 
bias in favour of Bihar. These figures  of employment clearly reveal the 
discrimination that has been done to Assam and the North-Eastern Region in 
NF Railway recruitment. With 9.28" per cent of NF Railway line in the State, 
Bihar enjoys 25.2 per cent of jobs in the 'C and 'D' categories, whereas Assam 
with 64.33 per cent of NF railway line has been given only 16.97 per cent jobs. If 
you look at the un-reserved posts also, the percentage comes further down to 10 
per cent. In the un-reserved posts, the percentage of employees from Assam and 
the North-Eastern Region is below 10. 
I, therefore, urge that in the interest of our national unity and integrity and in 
the interest of reducing the regional dis parities, this atrocious discrimination 
against Assam must end. I make this demand not only for Assam but also for the 
whole of the North-Eastern Region.
